title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page belongs to Grothendieck's 1966-67 notes on 'algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge'. These are abstract graded-commutative algebras modelling the cohomology of a smooth projective variety. They come with Poincaré duality, a Lefschetz class xi, and hard-Lefschetz and Hodge-index type axioms, and serve as a testing ground for the standard conjectures. Here he analyses the simplest non-trivial case: formal dimension 4 (a surface), with H^0 = k, H^1 = V, H^2 = k.xi + W, H^3 ≅ V^* by duality, H^4 = k.xi^2.

(1) Special case: (xy)(zt) = 0 for all x, y, z, t in H^1.
- He remarks that this is the same as (H^1)^3 = 0. This is correct by Poincaré duality: xyz in H^3 is zero iff xyz.t = 0 for all t in H^1.
- Equivalently, the image of the cup-product map alpha: Λ^2 V -> H^2 = k.xi + W is a totally isotropic subspace for the intersection form Q.
- Example. Take Q non-degenerate and W ≠ 0. If the field is large enough, e.g. algebraically closed, there is an isotropic line D in k.xi + W not contained in W = xi^⊥. Define alpha by a non-degenerate alternating form V x V -> D.
- Then the Lefschetz pairing phi(x, y) = Q(alpha(xy), xi) = xy.xi on H^1 is still non-degenerate. That is hard Lefschetz H^1 -> H^3, which is what 'phi sera aussi non dégénérée' means.
- Geometrically this models a ruled surface C x P^1, or more generally a surface whose H^1 comes from a curve. There all products of two 1-classes are multiples of the fibre class F, with F^2 = 0 and F.xi > 0.

(2) General case. Define the alternating 4-form chi by xyzt = chi(x, y, z, t) xi^2.
- The bilinear form induced on Λ^2 V by Q via alpha is Q(alpha(a), alpha(b)) = (ab) in H^4. It factors through Sym^2(Λ^2 V) -> Λ^4 V, i.e. it is the symmetric form chi'(a, b) = chi(a ∧ b).
- Hence a dimension-4 Poincaré algebra of this type is equivalent to the following data:
  - (a) a finite-dimensional vector space V;
  - (b) chi in (Λ^4 V)^*, giving a symmetric bilinear form chi' on Λ^2 V;
  - (c) a space W~ with a symmetric bilinear form Q~ and a linear map alpha: Λ^2 V -> W~ with alpha^*Q~ = chi';
  - (d) xi in W~ with Q(xi, xi) = 1.
- Non-degeneracy conditions: Q non-degenerate (Poincaré duality on H^2), and phi(x, y) = Q(alpha(xy), xi) non-degenerate (hard Lefschetz on H^1, which also gives the duality H^1 x H^3).
- The product H^1 x H^2 -> H^3 = V^* is then forced by duality. The data are designed for building or classifying abstract models, presumably to test which axioms are independent or to construct candidate counterexamples.

The positivity / Hodge-index axioms are not yet imposed on this page.
errors: No genuine mathematical errors. The bracket '(H^1)^3 = 0' is equivalent to (H^1)^4 = 0 only via Poincaré duality; Grothendieck's '!' signals exactly this.
Existence of the isotropic line D not in W needs a hypothesis on k, which he flags as 'si le corps ...'. Over R with a definite form it fails.
'Q ⊕ 1 (sur kξ + V)' should presumably read kξ + W, i.e. Q on W together with xi^2 = 1. The quantifier and characteristic-2 issues of Sym^2 vs alternating forms are ignored.

ideas.what: Equivalence (H^1)^4 = 0 ⇔ (H^1)^3 = 0 in a 4-dimensional Poincaré duality algebra; isotropy of the image of Λ^2 H^1 in H^2
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré duality argument; isotropic cup-product image (cf. surfaces fibred over curves / Castelnuovo-de Franchis type situations)

ideas.what: Example of a Poincaré-Lefschetz algebra in which alpha takes values in an isotropic line D not orthogonal to xi, so hard Lefschetz on H^1 holds while all 4-fold products vanish
ideas.modern_name: cohomology model of a ruled surface C x P^1 (fibre class F, F^2 = 0)

ideas.what: Description of a dimension-4 Poincaré duality algebra by data (V, chi in Λ^4V^*, (W~, Q~), alpha: Λ^2V -> W~ with alpha^*Q~ = chi', xi with Q(xi, xi) = 1), plus non-degeneracy of Q and of the Lefschetz pairing phi
ideas.modern_name: classification/realisation data for cohomology rings of closed 4-manifolds or surfaces (cup-product map Λ^2H^1 -> H^2 compatible with the intersection form); abstract Lefschetz/Kähler-type algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in 4-manifold topology and rational homotopy (various authors); abstract Hodge-Riemann/Lefschetz algebras later in combinatorial Hodge theory
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) states the conjectures but does not develop abstract Poincaré-Hodge algebras of this kind.

missed.claim: Evidence that in 1966-67 Grothendieck was systematically parametrising abstract 'Poincaré-Hodge' algebras of low dimension, starting with surfaces with H^1 ≠ 0, as a test bed for the standard conjectures. This program of axiomatic Lefschetz/Hodge-Riemann algebras was never published by him and resurfaced independently decades later (e.g. in combinatorial Hodge theory). The content of this page itself is elementary.
missed.quote: d'où les données a) V vect. ... b) χ : Λ^4 V → k ... c) un vectoriel W̃, avec une forme bil. sym. Q̃ ... d) un élément ξ de W̃, tel que Q(ξ,ξ) = 1. Conditions de non dégénérescence
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents an early abstract approach to Lefschetz and Hodge-index axioms that anticipates later 'Kähler package' axiomatics. No new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but elementary linear algebra: it parametrises 4-dimensional Poincaré-Lefschetz algebras and gives the isotropic (ruled-surface-like) example. Historically interesting as part of the unpublished Poincaré-Hodge algebra program, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Cas particulier [?] où' is likely 'Cas particulier: celui où (xy)(zt) = 0'.

The example reads roughly: 'Si Q non dégénérée, et supposons W ≠ 0, il existe (si le corps est ...) une droite isotrope D dans kξ + W qui n'est pas dans W, et on prendra α défini par une forme bilinéaire alternée non dégénérée de V × V dans D: alors φ sera aussi non dégénérée'. The transcription's 'φ sera aussi un isotrope' looks wrong; 'non dégénérée' fits the logic.
'Q ⊕ 1 (sur kξ + V)' should likely read 'sur kξ + W'.
'donc les données' should be 'd'où les données'.
In c), the bracket reads roughly '[i.e. telles que Q̃ induise via α la forme χ']', i.e. α compatible with χ' and Q.
